files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.EtlPipeline
files.Summary: Entry point for building a generic, format-agnostic ETL pipeline. Obtain a fresh builder with , start from a source — either a built-in From factory (see ) or a format-specific factory hung off the instance by a format package — append transformer stages on , terminate with a sink, then call .

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.EtlPipelineProgress
files.Summary: An immutable snapshot of a generic run's throughput, reported through the sink passed to .

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.EtlPipelineSinkExtensions
files.Summary: Extensions for terminal pipelines.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.EtlPipelineSourceExtensions
files.Summary: Built-in source factories for . They begin a pipeline from a raw stream or an extractor. Format packages add their own class-named source factories (for example CsvExtractor) as extension methods on alongside these, so every source reads the same way: EtlPipeline.Create().Xxx(...).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ExtractorBase<TSource>
files.Summary: A convenience that reports progress with the built-in type and supplies a default , so a derived extractor only has to implement ExtractWorkerAsync. Use this instead of the two-type-parameter base when you don't need a custom progress-report type — it removes the progress-record and CreateProgressReport boilerplate. Override if you want to enrich the report (for example set a known total).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ExtractorBase<TSource, TProgress>
files.Summary: Provides a basic implementation for data extractors that extract data of type TSource. Library authors can use this base class to create custom extractors by inheriting from it and implementing ExtractWorkerAsync and CreateProgressReport methods.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IEtlPipeline<T>
files.Summary: A generic, format-agnostic ETL pipeline carrying a stream of items of type T. Append transformer stages with , then terminate with (or a format-specific sink terminator) to obtain a runnable .

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IEtlPipelineSink
files.Summary: A terminated, runnable generic ETL pipeline. Obtained from or a format-specific sink terminator (for example a CsvLoader extension shipped by a format package).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractAsync<TSource>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous extractor interface for extracting data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the first step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractStage<TSource>
files.Summary: Represents the extractor stage of a fluent ETL pipeline for items of type TSource. Call one of the Transform overloads to append a transformer, or one of the Load overloads to terminate the chain with a loader.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractStageWithProgress<TSource, TProgress>
files.Summary: An whose underlying extractor also supports progress reporting. Call to supply an sink that will be forwarded to the extractor's ExtractAsync overload when the pipeline runs.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractWithCancellationAsync<TSource>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous extractor interface for extracting data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the first step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractWithProgressAndCancellationAsync<TSource, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous extractor interface for extracting data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the first step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IExtractWithProgressAsync<TSource, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous extractor interface for extracting data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the first step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IItemMiddleware<T>
files.Summary: A composable, reusable hook for cross-cutting per-item behaviour (logging, validation, metrics, throttling, deduplication) that can be attached to any stream without modifying the extractor, transformer, or loader that produced it. Attach one or more with ; they run in the order attached, each seeing the item the previous one passed on.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ILoadAsync<TDestination>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous loader interface for loading data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the last step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ILoadWithCancellationAsync<TDestination>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous loader interface for loading data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the last step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ILoadWithProgressAndCancellationAsync<TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous loader interface for loading data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the last step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ILoadWithProgressAsync<TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous loader interface for loading data of type T. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the last step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IPipeline
files.Summary: A terminated, runnable ETL pipeline. Obtained from an or Load overload.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IPipelineWithLoadProgress<TProgress>
files.Summary: An whose loader supports progress reporting. Call to supply an sink that will be forwarded to the loader's LoadAsync overload when the pipeline runs.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IProgressTimer
files.Summary: Represents a timer that raises at a regular interval, used by extractor, transformer, and loader base classes to drive progress callbacks.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.IReportsItemErrors
files.Summary: Implemented by an ETL stage that counts items its error policy discarded, so a pipeline can read that count uniformly regardless of the stage's concrete type. , , and all implement it, and EtlPipeline sums across every stage that reports it into .

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ISupportDryRun
files.Summary: Implemented by ETL stages that support a dry run — a mode in which the full pipeline is exercised but the external side effect that mutates a destination or source is skipped.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformAsync<TSource, TDestination>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous transformer interface for transforming data of type T to TResult. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the second step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformStage<TSource>
files.Summary: Represents a mid-chain stage of a fluent ETL pipeline whose current item type is TSource. Call one of the Transform overloads to append another transformer, or one of the Load overloads to terminate the chain.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformStageWithProgress<TSource, TProgress>
files.Summary: An whose underlying transformer also supports progress reporting. Call to supply an sink that will be forwarded to the transformer's TransformAsync overload when the pipeline runs.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformWithCancellationAsync<TSource, TDestination>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous transformer interface for transforming data of type T to TResult. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the second step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformWithProgressAndCancellationAsync<TSource, TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous transformer interface for transforming data of type T to TResult. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the second step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ITransformWithProgressAsync<TSource, TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Defines an asynchronous transformer interface for transforming data of type T to TResult. A class implementing this interface is intended to be the second step in an ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ItemErrorAction
files.Summary: The action a stage takes for an item that failed to process — returned by a stage's OnItemError policy and applied by the worker that called HandleItemError.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ItemErrorContext
files.Summary: Describes a single item that failed to process. It is passed to a stage's OnItemError policy so the policy can record the failure (a "dead letter") and decide whether to the item or the run.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.LoaderBase<TDestination>
files.Summary: A convenience that reports progress with the built-in type and supplies a default , so a derived loader only has to implement LoadWorkerAsync. Use this instead of the two-type-parameter base when you don't need a custom progress-report type — it removes the progress-record and CreateProgressReport boilerplate. Override if you want to enrich the report (for example set a known total).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.LoaderBase<TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Provides a basic implementation for data loaders that write data of type TDestination to a target destination. Library authors can use this base class to create custom loaders by inheriting from it and implementing LoadWorkerAsync and CreateProgressReport methods.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.MiddlewareExtensions
files.Summary: Extension methods that attach to an stream, so cross-cutting per-item behaviour composes onto any extractor / transformer output or loader input — and inside an EtlPipeline via Through(stream => stream.WithMiddleware(...)) — without changing the component itself.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.MiddlewareResult<T>
files.Summary: The outcome of running a single item through an : the (possibly replaced) item to pass on, and whether the item should be dropped from the stream. Create one with to keep an item flowing or to discard it.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.MiddlewareResult
files.Summary: Factory methods for creating values from an implementation.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.Pipeline
files.Summary: Entry point for building a fluent ETL pipeline. Start with one of the Extract overloads, chain zero or more Transform calls, terminate with one of the Load overloads, then invoke .

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.Report
files.Summary: Provides a point-in-time snapshot of the progress of an ETL process — how many items have been processed, how long it has been running, and (when the total is known) how far along it is and how much longer it is expected to take.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.TransformerBase<TSource, TDestination>
files.Summary: A convenience that reports progress with the built-in type and supplies a default , so a derived transformer only has to implement TransformWorkerAsync. Use this instead of the three-type-parameter base when you don't need a custom progress-report type — it removes the progress-record and CreateProgressReport boilerplate. Override if you want to enrich the report (for example set a known total).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.TransformerBase<TSource, TDestination, TProgress>
files.Summary: Provides a basic implementation for data transformers that convert data from TSource to TDestination. Library authors can use this base class to create custom transformers by inheriting from it and implementing TransformWorkerAsync and CreateProgressReport methods.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.ErrorPolicies.ItemErrorPolicy
files.Summary:
Ready-made policies for an ETL stage's error handling. Each is a
<xref href="System.Func%602" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> from an <xref href="Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ItemErrorContext" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> to an
<xref href="Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions.ItemErrorAction" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>, so it can be assigned directly to a stage's <code>ErrorPolicy</code>
property (on <code>ExtractorBase</code> / <code>LoaderBase</code> / <code>TransformerBase</code>):

<example><pre><code class="lang-csharp">var deadLetters = new List<ItemErrorContext>();

var extractor = new SomeExtractor<Record>(source) { ErrorPolicy = ItemErrorPolicy.SkipDeadLetterAndLog(deadLetters, logger) };

The dead-letter overloads write to a caller-owned sink (a collection or a channel), so its size —
and therefore the memory a bad feed can consume — stays under the caller's control.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.DelayingExtractor<T>
files.Summary: An extractor double that waits a configurable delay before yielding each item, simulating a latent / backpressured source. Useful for exercising timeout, cancellation-promptness, and progress-cadence behaviour that an instantaneous in-memory source cannot.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.FaultyExtractor<T>
files.Summary: An in-memory extractor for testing error-handling paths. It yields items from an like a normal extractor, but can be configured to inject deterministic faults — throwing at a given item, throwing after completion, or duplicating an item — so consumers can exercise mid-stream failure, finalization failure, and de-duplication logic without hand-rolling broken fakes.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.FaultyLoader<T>
files.Summary: An in-memory loader for testing error-handling paths. It consumes the source stream like a normal loader, but can be configured to inject deterministic faults — throwing at a given item, throwing after completion, or duplicating an item — so consumers can exercise mid-stream failure, finalization failure, and idempotency logic without hand-rolling broken fakes.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.FaultyTransformer<T>
files.Summary: A pass-through transformer for testing error-handling paths. It returns each item unchanged like a normal transformer, but can be configured to inject deterministic faults — throwing at a given item, throwing after completion, or duplicating an item — so consumers can exercise mid-stream failure, finalization failure, and de-duplication logic without hand-rolling broken fakes.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.ManualProgressTimerCore
files.Summary: A manually-driven progress timer for tests: instead of a real firing on an interval, the stage's progress callback fires only when is called, making progress-callback assertions deterministic. Attach it to a stage with (and the loader / transformer overloads).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.ManualTimeSource
files.Summary: A controllable time source for tests: time stands still until is called, making a stage's timing metrics — , , , and — deterministic rather than wall-clock-dependent.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.ProgressTimerExtensions
files.Summary: Extension methods that attach a to a stage so its progress callback fires deterministically (on ) instead of on a real timer interval.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.RecordingMiddleware<T>
files.Summary: A test that records every item passed through it and, by default, keeps each item flowing. Supply a policy to transform or drop items, and inspect to assert exactly what the middleware saw, in order.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.RetryingExtractor<T>
files.Summary: An extractor double that throws a transient fault on its first failFirstAttempts worker invocations and then succeeds, driven through a retry override of the 0.20 WrapWorkerExecution resilience seam. It both demonstrates how to build stream-level retry on a stage and serves as the reference component exercised by RetryContractTests (in Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.Xunit).

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.SnapshotTestLoader<T>
files.Summary: An in-memory loader that captures every item it receives and renders them as a single, deterministic, diff-friendly string — ready to hand to an approval / snapshot-testing framework such as Verify.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.TestExtractor<T>
files.Summary: An in-memory extractor for use in tests, examples, and benchmarks. Yields items from an , an , or a factory delegate, depending on which constructor is used.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.TestLoader<T>
files.Summary: A simple in-memory loader for use in tests, examples, and benchmarks. Iterates all items from the source stream and, when constructed with collectItems: true, makes them available via after the load completes.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.TestTransformer<T>
files.Summary: A pass-through transformer for use in tests, examples, and benchmarks. Returns each item unchanged, with no transformation applied.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.TimeSourceExtensions
files.Summary: Extension methods that attach a to a stage so its timing metrics can be driven deterministically in tests.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.Xunit.AllocationBudgetContractTests<TSut>
files.Summary: Opt-in xUnit contract-test base asserting that a repeatable operation's hot path stays within a declared per-item allocation budget — so a downstream author can lock in that their own extractor / loader / transformer keeps an allocation-free (or below-a-declared-N) hot path.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.Xunit.CancellationContractTests<TSut>
files.Summary: Abstract base class providing xUnit contract tests that verify a stage honours cancellation promptly — it stops shortly after the token is cancelled rather than draining its source, throws , and processes nothing when handed an already-cancelled token.

files.Title: Wolfgang.Etl.TestKit.Xunit.CancellationOutcome
